covers: The registers of the MC6845 CRT controller

entries.name: R0 horizontal total
entries.description: Horizontal total: the length of a scan line in characters.
entries.behaviour: Holds the number of character times in a horizontal period, less one, in 8 bits.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X reads back the value written; MAME returns 0, as the chip's registers are write only.

entries.name: R1 horizontal displayed
entries.description: Horizontal displayed: how many characters of a line are shown.
entries.behaviour: Holds the number of characters displayed per line, in 8 bits.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X reads back the value written; MAME returns 0, as the chip's registers are write only.

entries.name: R2 horizontal sync pos
entries.description: Horizontal sync position: the character at which the horizontal sync starts.
entries.behaviour: Holds the character position of the horizontal sync pulse, in 8 bits.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X reads back the value written; MAME returns 0, as the chip's registers are write only.

sources.ref: rbil61:PORTS.B CRT register 02h horizontal sync position

entries.name: R3 sync widths
entries.description: Sync widths: how long the horizontal sync lasts, and on some chips the vertical sync.
entries.behaviour: Bits 3 to 0 give the horizontal sync width in characters, 0 meaning 16. Bits 7 to 4 give the vertical sync width in lines on chips that have it; the others use 16.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X reads back the horizontal width only (Tandy also the vertical one) and fixes the vertical sync at 16 lines elsewhere; MAME reads back 0.

sources.ref: rbil61:PORTS.B CRT register 03h sync pulse width

entries.name: R4 vertical total
entries.description: Vertical total: the number of character rows in a frame.
entries.behaviour: Holds the number of character rows per frame, less one, in 7 bits.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X reads back the value written; MAME returns 0, as the chip's registers are write only.

entries.name: R5 vertical total adjust
entries.description: Vertical total adjust: extra scan lines added to the frame.
entries.behaviour: Holds the number of extra scan lines that complete the frame, in 5 bits.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X reads back the value written; MAME returns 0, as the chip's registers are write only.

sources.ref: rbil61:PORTS.B CRT register 05h vertical total adjust

entries.name: R6 vertical displayed
entries.description: Vertical displayed: how many character rows are shown.
entries.behaviour: Holds the number of character rows displayed, in 7 bits.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X reads back the value written; MAME returns 0, as the chip's registers are write only.

entries.name: R7 vertical sync pos
entries.description: Vertical sync position: the character row at which the vertical sync starts.
entries.behaviour: Holds the character row of the vertical sync pulse, in 7 bits.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X reads back the value written; MAME returns 0, as the chip's registers are write only.

entries.name: R8 interlace and skew
entries.description: Interlace and skew: the scan mode and the display and cursor skew.
entries.behaviour: Bits 1 and 0 select the interlace mode, 3 being interlace and video; bit 2 row and column addressing; bit 4 display enable skew; bit 5 cursor skew. Bits 3, 6 and 7 serve the variants with transparent update, and MAME logs a nonzero value as unsupported on chips without it.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X has no handler for it and logs a write as an illegal index; MAME stores the byte.

entries.name: R9 maximum raster
entries.description: Maximum raster address: the scan lines of a character row.
entries.behaviour: Holds the number of scan lines per character row, less one, in 5 bits.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X reads back the value written; MAME returns 0, as the chip's registers are write only.

sources.ref: rbil61:PORTS.B CRT register 09h maximum scan lines

entries.name: R10 cursor start
entries.description: Cursor start: the first scan line of the cursor and how it blinks.
entries.behaviour: Bits 4 to 0 give the first cursor scan line. Bits 6 and 5 select the cursor mode: 00 always on, 01 off, 10 blinking fast, 11 blinking slowly.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X keeps and reads back bits 5 to 0 and enables the cursor in every mode but 01; MAME keeps bits 6 to 0, applies all four modes, and returns 0 on a read, as the registers are write only.

entries.name: R11 cursor end
entries.description: Cursor end: the last scan line of the cursor.
entries.behaviour: Holds the last scan line of the cursor, in 5 bits.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X reads back the value written; MAME returns 0, as the chip's registers are write only.

entries.name: R12 start address high
entries.description: Start address high: the high byte of the first display address.
entries.behaviour: A write sets the high 6 bits of the address of the first displayed character.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X reads back the start address; MAME does so only on variants that allow it and returns 0 on the base chip.

sources.ref: rbil61:PORTS.B CRT register 0Ch start address high

entries.name: R13 start address low
entries.description: Start address low: the low byte of the first display address.
entries.behaviour: A write sets the low 8 bits of the address of the first displayed character.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X reads back the start address; MAME does so only on variants that allow it and returns 0 on the base chip.

sources.ref: rbil61:PORTS.B CRT register 0Dh start address low

against.ref: rbil61:PORTS.B CRT register 0Dh start address low

entries.name: R14 cursor high
entries.description: Cursor address high: the high byte of the cursor position.
entries.behaviour: A write sets the high 6 bits of the cursor address and a read returns them.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X keeps all 8 bits of a write to it; MAME keeps 6.

sources.ref: rbil61:PORTS.B CRT register 0Eh cursor location high

entries.name: R15 cursor low
entries.description: Cursor address low: the low byte of the cursor position.
entries.behaviour: A write sets the low 8 bits of the cursor address and a read returns them.

sources.ref: rbil61:PORTS.B CRT register 0Fh cursor location low

against.ref: rbil61:PORTS.B CRT register 0Fh cursor location low

entries.name: R16 light pen high
entries.description: Light pen high: the high byte of the address latched by the light pen.
entries.behaviour: A read returns the high byte of the latched light pen address and clears the latched flag. The register is read only.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X lets a write store the value (6 bits) and keeps no latched flag; MAME ignores a write.

sources.ref: rbil61:PORTS.B CRT register 10h light pen high
sources.cites: 10h R-	light pen high (MDA/CGA/EGA only, some HGC, few VGA

entries.name: R17 light pen low
entries.description: Light pen low: the low byte of the address latched by the light pen.
entries.behaviour: A read returns the low byte of the latched light pen address and clears the latched flag. The register is read only.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X lets a write store the value and keeps no latched flag; MAME ignores a write.

sources.ref: rbil61:PORTS.B CRT register 11h light pen low
sources.cites: 11h R- light pen low (MDA/CGA/EGA only, some HGC, few VGA

entries.name: R18 update addr high
entries.description: Update address high: the high byte of the address a transparent update writes.
entries.behaviour: On variants with transparent update, a write sets the high 6 bits of the update address. The base chip ignores it.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X has no handler for it and logs an illegal index; MAME handles it on the variants with transparent update.

entries.name: R19 update addr low
entries.description: Update address low: the low byte of the address a transparent update writes.
entries.behaviour: On variants with transparent update, a write sets the low 8 bits of the update address. The base chip ignores it.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X has no handler for it and logs an illegal index; MAME handles it on the variants with transparent update.

entries.name: R31 update strobe
entries.description: Update strobe: a read or write of it triggers a transparent update.
entries.behaviour: On variants with transparent update, any access performs the update; the other chips ignore it.
entries.differs: DOSBox-X has no handler for it and logs an illegal index; MAME handles it on the variants with transparent update.
